name: Guerrero sling materials
aliases: TVT versus Pelvicol versus autologous fascial sling
question: How do retropubic TVT, Pelvicol porcine dermis, and autologous fascial slings compare for primary surgery in women with urodynamic stress urinary incontinence?

design.blinding: Patients and outcome-collecting research nurses masked; fascial harvest incision could reveal assignment
design.population: Women in four UK units requiring primary surgery for urodynamically proven stress urinary incontinence.
design.description: Four-center, three-arm superiority randomized trial; 211 randomized, 201 treated
design.locator: Full text, Methods and Figure 1, pp 1494–1496

verdictNote: No six-week difference; Pelvicol had lower later improvement; TVT–fascia comparison was underpowered.
takeaway: Among 201 treated women, six-week improvement was similar after retropubic TVT, Pelvicol porcine dermis, and autologous fascia (91%, 91%, and 94% among respondents); Pelvicol had lower improvement at six and 12 months.

delivery.label: Assigned sling techniques
delivery.value: All slings placed mid-urethrally by experienced surgeons with standardized steps. Pelvicol used a 12 × 2 cm porcine graft on 1.0 nylon threads passed retropubically (bottom-up); the autologous sling used an 8–10 × 1.5 cm rectus-fascia graft via a Pfannenstiel incision, with the same retropubic passage. Cystoscopy followed every sling insertion.

delivery.label: Pelvicol arm suspension
delivery.value: Pelvicol recruitment stopped after the planned interim analysis found significantly poorer improvement and dry rates; TVT and AFS recruitment continued until slowing enrollment closed the trial.
